findings.message: the connector directory this run was captured with is not one this build ships: the receipt claims ed4d5103762d0093d29f5d5ecafd08586295e92191e2e192a2aab672bd723fa5 for `codex-cli`, and no directory pin of this build's has that digest. the daemon renders the hook bodies under `files/` into the workspace, records their rendered digests as the config it will guard, and then guards them — so an edited template is not a file that slipped past a check, it is the file every later check agrees with. evidence.note: key source: pinned, and the key is the M1 placeholder

findings.message: the key that verified this trace's server signatures is the M1 placeholder anchor, whose private seed is published in this repository so the fixtures can sign with it. Anybody can mint a receipt or an acknowledgement under it, so a `key_source` of `pinned` says only that the signature matched a key everyone holds. Replacing the placeholder with the real organiser key is the release gate before any entry is judged

3 record(s) and post(s) sit in the 300s arming window below `started_at` (2026-09-08T04:26:37Z). This is what a run arming itself looks like: the connector's arming signal is the harness's own first output, so the records that CAUSE the start receipt to be requested are chained before the request goes out. They carry no work — the baseline the receipt witnessed is seq 0, below all of them — so they are counted here rather than failed
